newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee up.
newsitem.headline: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee up.

text.p: High call rates helped the Sri Lanka rupee to regain ground lost when the dollar rose during mid-day, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.73 to the dollar, after opening at 57.80 and rising to 57.85. The rupee closed at 57.80 on Tuesday.
"The dollar rose to a high of 57.85 rupees around mid-day when speculators bought on the overseas strength of the U.S. currency," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
"But the dollar fell back as money was high throughout," he said. Call rates closed at 20 percent after moving between 17 and 22 percent, during the day.
Call rates are expected to ease later this week, after the Central Bank bought 1.5 billion rupees worth of Treasury Bills at today's auction, which was under-subscribed, dealers said.
Money became tight as banks had covered imports with dollars from the Central Bank since last Thursday, they said.
